newsitem.title: USA: Judge asked to toss out Orange County indictment.
newsitem.headline: Judge asked to toss out Orange County indictment.

text.p: Former Orange County, Calif., Assistant Treasurer Matthew Raabe has asked a judge to dismiss charges stemming from the county's financial crisis and bankruptcy, his attorneys said Tuesday.
As expected, defense attorneys filed a motion to dismiss the indictment, which alleged Raabe made false statements in the sale of securities and misappropriated public funds.
In their motion to dismiss, Raabe's attorneys argued that the fund diversions were not illegal because the county had the right to set investment pool returns.
Raabe's long-awaited trial got underway last month.

The prosecution, which rested its case last week, alleged that Raabe concealed the fund diversions from the county-run investment portfolio as well as the risky investments that led to the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
The defense was expected to begin presenting its case in court as early as Thursday. Raabe, who has denied any wrongdoing, faces up to 12 years in prison.
His trial could last until mid-May, attorneys said.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Raabe was one of several Orange County officials to face charges following the bankruptcy.

In April 1995, former Orange County Treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis. A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work program instead of jail.
Citron claimed that Raabe was the "mastermind" behind the scheme to divert interest earnings.
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
